content.thinking:
All warmup! Because with 64 connections sharing 4 slots, every packet causes a slot reset (different connection), so the window never fills. I need to design the stress test so that the same connection sends consecutive packets. Let me restructure: use runs of packets per connection, or fewer connections than slots.

Let me use slots=256, 64 connections with distinct slots, so no collisions.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && sed -i 's/"slots": S, "window"/"slots": 256, "window"/; s/"slot": i % S,/"slot": i % 256,/' tmp/stress_gen.py && python3 tmp/stress_gen.py tmp/stress.json && time python3 submission/main.py < tmp/stress.json > tmp/stress_out.json && python3 -c '
import json, collections
o=json.load(open("tmp/stress_out.json"))
print("jobs",len(o["jobs"]))
print(collections.Counter(p["decision"] for p in o["packets"]))
print(collections.Counter(j["status"] for j in o["jobs"]))
' && ls -l tmp/stress_out.json
